'''Bilge Demirköz''' (born 1980) is a Turkish professor of high energy physics at [[Middle East Technical University]]. She coordinates the ''Particle Radiation Tests Creation Laboratory'', the first collaboration between Turkey and [[CERN]], the European Organization for Nuclear Research.

== Education and career ==
Demirköz is from Istanbul.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://demirkoz.web.cern.ch/demirkoz/|title=Bilge Demirkoz|website=demirkoz.web.cern.ch|access-date=2018-10-15}}</ref> She attended [[Robert College]] for her high school studies. She wanted to take part in research during her undergraduate degree, so moved to [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://www.metu.edu.tr/researchers/assoc-prof-dr-bilge-demirkoz-department-physics-metu|title=Assoc. Prof. Dr. Bilge Demirköz, Department of Physics, METU|date=2013-01-08|work=METU - Middle East Technical University|access-date=2018-10-15|language=en}}</ref> She won Joel Matthew Orloff Award in 2001.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://web.mit.edu/physics/current/awards/index.html|title=MIT Department of Physics|website=web.mit.edu|access-date=2018-10-15}}</ref> She earned a [[Bachelor of Science]] in Physics and Music from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 2001.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.physics.metu.edu.tr/Admission/ADM-139|title=Phys : Melahat Bilge Demirköz|website=www.physics.metu.edu.tr|access-date=2018-10-15}}</ref> She started working on the [[Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer]]. She was offered PhD positions in [[California Institute of Technology]], [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], [[Stanford University]] and [[Harvard University]].<ref name=":0" /> Despite originally starting her PhD at MIT, the [[Space Shuttle Columbia disaster]] resulted in her moving to the [[University of Oxford]].<ref name=":0" /> She was a [[Science and Technology Facilities Council]] Dorothy Hodgkin Scholar under the supervision of [[Antony Weidberg]]. She completed her postgraduate studies at the [[University of Oxford]] in 2007, and was a member of [[Balliol College, Oxford|Balliol College]].<ref name=":1" /> Her thesis was titled ''Construction and Performance of the ATLAS SCT Barrels and Cosmic Tests''.<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Melahat|first=Demirkoz, Bilge|date=2007|title=Construction and Performance of the ATLAS SCT Barrels and Cosmic Tests|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1078223?ln=en|journal=CERN Document Server|language=en}}</ref>

From 2007 to 2009 Demirköz was a postdoctoral fellow at [[CERN]]<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Phys : Melahat Bilge Demirköz|url=http://www.physics.metu.edu.tr/Admission/ADM-139|access-date=2021-12-03|website=www.physics.metu.edu.tr}}</ref> where she worked for the [[ATLAS experiment]].<ref name="111th ACCU Meeting">{{Cite journal|date=2016-02-25|title=111th ACCU Meeting|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/2134484|journal=CERN Document Server|language=en}}</ref> In 2009, she was a postdoctoral scholar at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name=":4" /> from 2009 until 2011, she was a postdoctoral fellow at CERN and the Institute for High Energy Physics (Institut de Fisica d'Altes Energies ([[IFAE]]).<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Bilge Demirköz {{!}} SU Gender|url=https://sugender.sabanciuniv.edu/en/bilge-demirk%C3%B6z|access-date=2018-10-15|website=sugender.sabanciuniv.edu|language=en|archive-date=2018-10-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181016032901/https://sugender.sabanciuniv.edu/en/bilge-demirk%C3%B6z|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":4" /> 

She was promoted to Professor at [[Middle East Technical University]] in 2017. She serves as the [[Principal investigator|Principal Investigator]] of the astroparticle physics group.

== Research ==
Demirköz is an astro-particle physicist who is known for her research on space radiation and particles that travel close to the speed of light.<ref name=":3" /> Her research includes work on the jet shapes of 900 GeV and 7 TeV data from the [[ATLAS experiment]], testing detectors  using cosmic rays,<ref name=":0" /> and participating in the [[Alpha Magnetic Spectrometer]] experiment on the [[International Space Station]].<ref name=":2" /> She founded the [[Engin Arık|Engin Arik]] Fellowship in 2008, a fund which supports Turkish students at [[CERN]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://atlas-service-enews.web.cern.ch/atlas-service-enews/2007-8/features_07-8/features_engin.php|title=ATLAS e-News {{!}} Features|website=atlas-service-enews.web.cern.ch|access-date=2018-10-15}}</ref> She leads the ''Particle Radiation Tests Creation Laboratory'', the first collaboration between Turkey and [[CERN]]. This allows her to study the radiation environment of the earth as well as monitoring the impact of radiation on electronic devices.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://globalyoungacademy.net/bilge-demirkoz/|title=Bilge Demirkoz|work=Global Young Academy|access-date=2018-10-15|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2021, Demirköz led the team that developed a radiation meter that is the first scientific payload to go to from Turkey to space.<ref>{{Cite web|date=November 24, 2021|title=Kanal B - Türkiye'nin ilk bilimsel görev yükü 'Radyasyon Ölçer' GUHEM'de sergilenecek|url=http://www.kanalb.com.tr/haber.php?HaberNo=151405|access-date=2021-12-03|website=www.kanalb.com.tr}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
She was selected as a [[TED fellow]] in 2011.<ref name="111th ACCU Meeting" />{{Failed verification|date=November 2025|reason=cited source on the ACCU meeting does not mention anything about TED fellowship}} She was appointed to the [[CERN]] User Advisory Committee in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Sciences|first=Turkish Academy of|title=TÜBA Association Member Associate Professor Dr. M. Bilge Demirköz has been appointed to CERN User's Advisory Committee {{!}} Turkish Academy of Sciences|url=http://www.tuba.gov.tr/en/news/about-academy/tuba-association-member-associate-professor-dr.-m.-bilge-demirkoz-has-been-appointed-to-cern-users-advisory-committee|access-date=2018-10-15|website=www.tuba.gov.tr|language=en}}</ref> Demirköz has served on the Board of the Arts at [[CERN]]. Demirköz was elected to the [[Turkish Academy of Sciences]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bilge Demirköz {{!}} Turkish Academy of Sciences|url=http://www.tuba.gov.tr/en/members/all-members/principal-members/bilge-demirkoz-1|access-date=2021-12-02|website=www.tuba.gov.tr}}</ref>  In 2015 she spoke at the Turkish Women's Network.<ref>{{Citation|last=TurkishWIN|title=M. Bilge Demirköz {{!}} Finding Dark Matter in a Whiteout|date=2015-01-13|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Iqv-MzaFrWo|access-date=2018-10-15}}</ref> She was named a [[L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards|L'Oréal-UNESCO]] International Rising Talent in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Turkish woman scientist Bilge Demirköz to receive UNESCO grant|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-woman-scientist-bilge-demirkoz-to-receive-unesco-grant-110601|access-date=2018-10-15|website=Hürriyet Daily News|date=9 March 2017 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=The l'Oréal Foundation and UNESCO recognize 15 young women researchers for their outstanding contribution to science|url=https://en.unesco.org/news/oreal-foundation-and-unesco-recognize-15-young-women-researchers-their-outstanding-contribution|access-date=2018-10-15|website=UNESCO|language=en}}</ref> In 2017, she received a [[British Council]] professional achievement alumni award,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alumni Award winners 2017|url=https://study-uk.britishcouncil.org/alumni-awards/winners/2017|url-status=live|access-date=December 2, 2021|website=British Council|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190821055804/https://study-uk.britishcouncil.org/alumni-awards/winners/2017 |archive-date=2019-08-21 }}</ref> and was nominated to the [[Global Young Academy]].<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web|last=Sciences|first=Turkish Academy of|title=TÜBA Associate Member Assoc. Prof. Demirköz Selected as Member of GYA {{!}} Turkish Academy of Sciences|url=http://www.tuba.gov.tr/en/news/about-academy/tuba-associate-member-assoc.-prof.-demirkoz-selected-as-member-of-gya|access-date=2018-10-15|website=www.tuba.gov.tr|language=en}}</ref> She was featured in the 2018 [[Science Magazine]] celebration of women in science,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Let's talk (women in science) - SRI Magazine 2018 - Sunnybrook Research Institute|url=https://sunnybrook.ca/research/content/?page=sri-magazine-2018-lets-talk|access-date=2018-10-15|website=sunnybrook.ca|language=en}}</ref> and was elected to the [[Young Global Leaders]] forum in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|last=sabah|first=daily|date=2019-03-14|title=Turkish scientist Demirköz selected as Young Global Leader by WEF|url=https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/2019/03/14/turkish-scientist-demirkoz-selected-as-young-global-leader-by-wef|access-date=2021-12-03|website=Daily Sabah|language=en-US}}</ref>
